thread:
Maria: Heads-up — bringing up orenda-10b for product search. Did a quick INT8 run and seeing a small quality delta on our long-form recall slice (~2.8% drop on R@10). Need a concise cost-vs-quality decision to present to GTN by EOD tomorrow.
Ajay: can you paste the eval slice numbers? rough econ delta?
Maria: quick numbers: FP16 baseline cost per 1k tokens (in our infra) = $0.42. INT8 cost = $0.12. Raw unit saving ~71%. But on the longform recall slice latency p95 went from 210ms -> 260ms (INT8 on the same instance) and R@10 dropped 2.8%.
Drew: 2.8% R@10 drop is material for Search. Do we have prompt-level regressions or specific categories?
Maria: eyeballing the slice it’s concentrated on multi-turn context >1024 tokens and queries with code blocks. Single-turn QA looks fine.
Taylor: what's our cost target if we roll INT8? product wanted 40% token cost reduction to consider moving to Dedicated. This is more like 70% though, which is attractive.
Ajay: proposal: run an A/B canary with routing weight 90% FP16, 10% INT8 for 48h on a representative traffic shard. Metrics to track: R@10, R@1, MRR, latency p50/p95, downstream CTR, and failure-rate. Also run synthetic adversarial set with 500 examples for the code-block cases.
Maria: agreed. Also add a signal for "fidelity-drop": if any metric drops >1.5% absolute vs baseline on the canary, auto-rollback.
Drew: add per-prompt heatmap + sample dump for any failures so ML can triage quickly.
Taylor: product ask — include unit econ delta: show cost per 1k tokens and cost per successful retrieval (approx). If INT8 reduces cost by 70% but drops R@10 by 2.8%, what's net cost per successful retrieval change?
Ajay: quick back-of-envelope: baseline cost per 1k tokens $0.42, R@10 ~0.72 -> cost per success ~0.58. INT8: cost $0.12, R@10 ~0.70 -> cost per success ~0.17. Net ~70% lower cost per success despite quality drop. Need to present to GTN with caveats.
Maria: good. But product will worry about edge-case severity. Suggest hybrid routing: default INT8, fallback FP16 for contexts >1024 tokens or if prompt matches code-block regex.
Taylor: hybrid makes sense. Could we implement a quick routing rule? example: if tokens_prompt > 1024 -> route to fp16. Also include a flag for regex on triple-backtick.
Maria: sample rule (routing config):
```json
{"routing_rules": [{"name":"long_context_fp16","condition": "ctx_len > 1024","route":"orenda-10b-fp16"},{"name":"codeblock_fp16","condition":"matches(prompt, /```/) ","route":"orenda-10b-fp16"},{"name":"default","route":"orenda-10b-int8"}]}
```
Drew: small note — INT8 p95 latency went up in our microbench because of fallback path into extra dequant steps when cache warms up. We should warm the kvcache for canary traffic or pre-warm with synthetic traffic to avoid noisy p95 spikes.
Ajay: I'll kick off the synthetic warmup script for the canary and run the adversarial 500 examples. Maria, can you set the canary in console with the routing rules? Taylor, can you prep the GTN slide with the econ numbers and the risk bullets?
Maria: will do. Setting canary: 1h ramp -> hold 48h -> 1h ramp down. Auto-rollback on fidelity-drop >1.5% or latency p95 degradation >30% relative.
Taylor: I'll draft slides and include suggested tradeoff matrix: 
- Option A: FP16 baseline (no regressions, higher cost)
- Option B: INT8 hybrid (default INT8, FP16 for long/code) (best cost/perf balance)
- Option C: INT8 default (max savings, higher product risk)

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-orenda-10b-int8 starting 2026-03-21T16:00Z. Monitor channel #incidents and #eng-ml for alerts. :rocket:
Maria: added a small eval scorecard to the console: fields = ["slice", "R@10_delta", "MRR_delta", "p95_latency_delta", "cost_per_1k_tokens", "cost_per_success"]. I'll share the link once canary is up.
Drew: thanks — when can we see initial numbers? after 4 hours of steady traffic should be enough for signal on common slices.
Ajay: running evals now, will post results in this thread.
Maria: thanks everyone. GTN prep tomorrow 11:00 PT. If we see any >1.5% fidelity-drop in first 4 hours we'll pause ramp and triage immediately. :+1:
